findings: BTZ_1.tex l.1574-1575 (« Using Corollary cor:intersect we deduce that Sigma* is a Cauchy surface of M* »), and l.1093 for the compact case. The paper gives no argument for infinitely many spears. The argument goes through, and is proved here (GX.E0SpearFamily.LFSurgeryData.isCauchySurface_sigmaStar), once the spear family is LOCALLY FINITE, a property the paper does not state (it says only « disjoint », l.1574). Local finiteness is used in three places: the union of the spears is closed; the closure of the union of the cusp half-spears is the union of their closures, which makes the two sides of Sigma* closed in Reg M; and near a point of a spear no other spear is met. This fills a gap. It is not a counterexample: I did not show that disjointness alone fails.

The compact proof (B21 l.1093; strict E0Surgery.SurgeryData.isCauchySurface_sigmaStar) uses the compactness of S twice: J^±(S) closed, and a limit point in S of points of S below a past- or future-trapped curve. A Cauchy surface of a globally hyperbolic E0-manifold needs neither. J^±(S) is closed (E0LM.sfa_isClosed_Jplus_cauchy / _Jminus_cauchy). J^-(p) ∩ S and J^+(p) ∩ S are compact (Causal.Causality.GloballyHyperbolic.isCompact_Jminus_inter_of_isCauchySurface, with the time function E0LM.e0_timeFunction), and the points of S below e(-n) all lie in J^-(e 0) ∩ S. So step (2) holds for every Cauchy surface S, compact or not, with no completeness and no smoothness beyond what the spear data carry.

« Corollary cor:intersect applied in each spear »: the Lean proof, like the strict one, does not invoke the intersection number (lem_intersect_number_complete) directly. It uses the monotone height of the cusp along ≼ in each spear chart (Lemma 2.7) together with Remark 2.12 (rem:curve_spear, the strict SpearSurgeryDatum.isSpearArc_of_inextensible, applied spear by spear). Remark 2.12 is therefore discharged here, not assumed: the strict theorem carries it as a hypothesis hrem.
questions: « Sigma* is a Cauchy surface of M* » (l.1574): read as in the strict compact case, i.e. (Causal.Flat.flatCausality 2 (e0RegMFlat M)).IsCauchySurface Dat.sigmaStarReg, with Sigma* = (S minus the spears) union the cusps, and Sigma* contained in Reg M (sigmaStar_subset_regM). The spear family carries the readings of T-btz-spear-family (OQ-146 (c)): an index type equivalent to S ∩ sing_0(M), S's trace on each spear the graph of tau_Sigma in the shaft, with a C¹ rim.

kb_proposals: Sigma* Cauchy in Reg M needs neither compactness nor finiteness: GX.E0SpearFamily.LFSurgeryData.isCauchySurface_sigmaStar takes (IsCauchySurface S) and a locally finite family. Finiteness is replaced by LocallyFinite.closure_iUnion / isClosed_iUnion and eventually_all_finite. Compactness of S is replaced by cauchy_facts_lf: J^±(S) closed (E0LM.sfa_isClosed_*_cauchy) and J^∓(p) ∩ S compact (GloballyHyperbolic.isCompact_J*_inter_of_isCauchySurface with E0LM.e0_timeFunction).

The strict E0Surgery.SurgeryData.isCauchySurface_sigmaStar's hS : IsE0C1SpacelikeCauchy and hrem are both stronger than needed: IsCauchySurface S suffices, and hrem is SpearSurgeryDatum.isSpearArc_of_inextensible applied spear by spear. A strict cleanup could restate it over LFSurgeryData, of which the finite SurgeryData is a case (sigmaStar_toSurgeryData is rfl).
